text: . In the Indian bullion market today, 24 carat gold was 1.4 per cent down at 1,52,703 per 10 grams. Meanwhile, Silver shed 1.6 per cent to 2,31,650 rupees per kilogram.

. Vultures are extremely important for our ecosystem. By feeding on dead animals, they help keep the environment clean and reduce the spread of harmful diseases.However, vulture populations have declined significantly because of habitat loss, poisoning, and certain veterinary medicines that are harmful to them. Conservation efforts are therefore essential to protect these birds and maintain the balance of nature.On this International Vulture Day, government and environmental experts have urged people to understand, protect, and conserve vultures for a healthier environment.

. The death toll from the devastating Nepal-Tibet flash floods has surged to 1,355, according to National Disaster Risk Reduction and Managment Authority.The highest number of fatalities have been reported in Chitwan at 363, followed by Nawalparasi East with 222, Nawalparasi West with 221, and Rasuwa with 169.  Security agencies have continued search and rescue operations for people who remain out of contact, particularly at hydropower projects along the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli river corridors.According to the Independent Power Producers’ Association, Nepal (IPPAN), a representative body of private-sector power developers in Nepal, as many as 919 people employed at 11 hydropower projects remained out of contact as of last evening.There have been a few successful rescues of people alive from some hydropower projects, including two Nepali nationals from the 60-MW Upper Trishuli 3A project on September 4 and a Chinese national from the 216-MW Upper Trishuli-1 project on September 5.A national day of mourning is being observed today in Nepal in honour of those who lost their lives in the devastating flood that struck the Bhote Koshi River in Rasuwa district on August 26.

. Reigning world champion Sheetal Devi has confirmed a medal for India by storming into the women’s compound individual final on the third day of the stage three of World Archery Para Series in Ahmedabad today.In an all-Indian semifinal, the armless archer from Jammu defeated Sarita 145-143 to book her place in the gold medal clash. She will face Aizada Seidan of Kazakhstan in the final.Sarita will also have another opportunity to add to India’s medal tally when she will take on Wang Huiting of China in the bronze medal match.The women’s compound event thus gave India one confirmed medal and another still in the hunt, with world number one Sheetal eyeing the top podium finish.In the W1 women’s section, second-seeded Indian Swati Chaudhary set to fight for the bronze medal. Swati lost to sixth seed Liu Jing of China 1-7.In the compound Men’s section, reigning world champion and world number one Toman Kumar lost to top seed Ken Swagumilang of Indonesia 146-144 in the semifinal. He will fight for the bronze medal against Abbas Kahdim of Iraq.However, India’s campaign ended in the W1 men’s section after fifth seed Adil Mohamed Nazir Ansari and ninth seed Nurudin lost their respective quarterfinal matches.Athletes classified as W1 usually have an impairment in the top and bottom halves of their bodies, torso and at least three limbs and some W1 athletes have an assistant to help them load the bow.

. Benchmark domestic equity indices ended half a per cent lower today. The Sensex declined 383 points to close at 76,133, while the Nifty shed 119 points to settle at 23,779.However, in the broader market at the National Stock Exchange, the Midcap 100 index fell half a per cent, while the Smallcap 100 index ended largely flat.Earlier, the markets opened marginally down amid elevated crude oil prices and renewed hostilities in West Asia. Both benchmark indices remained under pressure throughout the session, as a broad-based sell-off was witnessed across sectors.In the Sensex pack, 23 out of 30 companies logged losses. Among the top laggards, Infosys declined 3.8 per cent, Tech Mahindra lost two per cent and Tata Steel dipped 1.8 per cent. In contrast, Larsen and Toubro as well as Bharti Airtel gained 0.6 per cent, Maruti rose half a per cent and Power Grid added 0.4 per cent.In the sectoral indices on the BSE, 23 out of 28 sectors edged downward. Among the top underperformers, Focused IT lost 2.2 per cent, IT decreased 2.1 per cent and Realty as well as Insurance dropped 1.4 per cent. In contrast, Telecommunication rose 1.6 per cent, Healthcare added 0.7 per cent and Hospitals gained 0.4 per cent.The overall market breadth at the BSE was negative, as shares of 2571 companies declined, 1925 advanced and 233 remained unchanged.

. Russia and North Korea have opened the first road bridge across their shared border today. Russian officials hailed the development to boost nations’ deepening ties with North Korea. The Russian government said in a statement, the bridge over the Tumen River is a kilometre long and has two lanes. Relations and exchange programmes between Russia and North Korea have been flourishing in recent years, with North Korea supplying ammunition and troops to support Russia’s war against Ukraine. North Korea has been receiving Russian tourists since February 2024 amid slowly easing pandemic curbs

. The Greater Noida Industrial Development Authority (GNIDA) has proposed separating freight and passenger movement in Greater Noida and constructing a 105-metre-wide road up to the Hapur bypass to improve connectivity with the Ganga Expressway. The proposal was discussed at a meeting chaired by Industrial Development Minister Nand Gopal Gupta in Lucknow yesterday.Additional Chief Secretary, Industrial Development, Alok Kumar was also present at the meeting. GNIDA officials said the road would reduce the distance between Noida-Greater Noida and the Ganga Expressway to around 30 to 45 minutes. The statement said extending the connectivity by around 15 km would link Greater Noida with the Ganga Expressway. The authority also proposed a six-lane elevated road from the Multi Modal Logistics Hub (MMLH) to the Noida International Airport in Jewar.The proposed road, running parallel to the Western Dedicated Freight Corridor, is intended specifically for freight movement and would connect to the airport, so goods from the logistics hub can be transported directly to the air cargo terminal.

. The fourth United Nations Climate Week has opened in Azerbaijan’s capital, Baku today, weeks before COP31. Governments, Financial Institutions, Businesses and Climate Experts have come together for a five-day meeting being held till 11th of this month to deliberate upon climate action, finance, adaptation and transparency.On the opening day today, high-level dialogue on implementing the Paris Agreement’s Enhanced Transparency Framework took place. The framework requires countries to report progress on emissions cuts, adaptation and climate support.The dialogue, involving the presidencies of COP29 (Azerbaijan), COP30 (Brazil) and incoming COP31 (Turkey), is aimed at building political momentum for improved climate reporting and identifying gaps in support for developing countries. Other discussions during the week will address carbon markets, adaptation, just transition, nationally determined contributions and the mobilisation of finance for climate action.The discussions are also expected to feed into preparations for COP31, where governments will face pressure to strengthen climate plans and demonstrate progress under the Paris Agreement.Climate finance remains one of the most politically sensitive issues in the UN negotiations, particularly as developing nations argue that existing commitments fall far short of the resources needed for adaptation, clean energy and loss and damage caused by extreme weather.Baku Climate Action Week 2026 is being held alongside the UNFCCC gathering,  bringing together investors, businesses, civil society groups and other non-state actors.

. In Women’s Cricket, India will take on arch-rivals Pakistan in the final Group A clash of the T20 Asia Cup at the Dubai International Stadium tonight. The match will begin at 8 PM Indian Standard Time.India have already secured a place in the semi-finals after recording convincing victories over Thailand and Hong Kong in their previous two matches.The Indian team will now look to maintain its winning run and finish the group stage with a perfect record.Pakistan, meanwhile, have played just one match. They began their campaign with a win over Thailand.The team currently has two points in Group A and needs just one more point from its remaining two matches to qualify for the semi-finals. Their last league game is against Hong Kong.Last night, Hosts United Arab Emirates (UAE) defeated Indonesia by six wickets at the Dubai International Stadium. Chasing a target of 72 runs, the UAE overhauled the score, posting 75 for the loss of four wickets in 13.1 overs.Earlier, put in to bat, Indonesia were bowled out for 71 in 19.4 overs.

. The government has extended the last date for submission of applications by selected meritorious students for National Means cum Merit Scholarship Scheme (NMMSS) for 2026-27 to 30th September this year. The NMMSS is implemented through the National Scholarship Portal (NSP). Following the extension, the last date for Level-1 verification at the Institute Nodal Officer is 15th October while the last date for Level-2 verification with the District Nodal Officer is 31st October.The National Means-cum-Merit Scholarship Scheme awards scholarships to meritorious students from economically weaker sections to prevent drop-out of students after elementary level that is Class eight and encourage them to complete their school education up to higher secondary level that is Class 12. The scholarship amount is 12 thousand rupees per annum per student.The Scheme provides one lakh fresh scholarships every year for Class 9 students who clear the qualifying exam for the scholarship conducted by the State and UT governments. The scholarship is continued through renewal mode from Classes 10 to 12 based on the student’s academic performance. The scheme is applicable only to students studying in State Government, Government-aided and local body schools.The eligibility parameters for availing the scholarship include parental income of not more than 3.50 lakh rupees per annum, a minimum of 55 per cent marks or equivalent grade in the Class 8 examination for appearing in the selection test for award of scholarship. The government has advised all the eligible students to complete their scholarship applications on the National Scholarship Portal within the extended timeline.

. In football, India qualified for the AFC U20 Asian Cup main tournament for the first time in 20 years, after a 3-nil win over Bangladesh in their final qualifying match in Tashkent yesterday.In their final Group B qualifier, Danny Meitei Laishram opened the scoring in the 25th minute, before Vishal Yadav doubled India’s lead with an acrobatic finish on the hour mark. Substitute Md Arbash made it 3-nil in the 79th minute.The victory, India’s second in the qualifiers, took them to six points from three matches. India then waited for the result of the Syria-Uzbekistan match.Uzbekistan’s 3-nil win over Syria confirmed India’s qualification as one of the seven best runners-up across the eight groups. India last featured in the AFC U20 Asian Cup in 2006. Uzbekistan topped Group B with nine points, while Syria finished third with three points. Bangladesh, who lost all three matches, were relegated to the Development Phase.The AFC U20 Asian Cup will be held in China from 24th March to 10th April, next year.

. On the eve of Raksha Bandhan, President Droupadi Murmu has extended greetings to people. The President said that the festival of Raksha Bandhan has been an integral part of country’s culture and tradition since ancient times. She said that rakhi thread, tied around the wrist with faith, is regarded as a sacred bond of protection, known as Raksha Bandhan.The President  said that in many shlokas and mantras, Rakshe, Ma Chala, Ma Chala can be found which expresses the imploration that may this bond of protection continue forever. President Murmu urged every citizen to take a pledge to strengthen the bonds amongst families and communities, marching forward with this spirit towards a Viksit Bharat.Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla also extended greetings to countrymen on the eve of Raksha Bandhan. In his message, Mr Birla said festival that celebrates the mutual love, affection, and trust between brothers and sisters. He noted that the festival symbolizes of India’s rich culture, family values, and the unbreakable bonds of affection and belonging.

. Iran has raised gasoline prices for high-volume consumers, marking the second fuel-price increase since December as the country faces growing economic pressures.Iran’s state media reported that under the new system, people buying more than their quota of 110 litres (29 gallons) of gasoline a month, now must pay one lakh rials (about 7 cents) per liter, or twice as much as they have been paying since December. The move comes as Iran’s currency continues to weaken and purchasing power declines. Experts warn that higher fuel prices could lead higher inflation, that’s already struggling with an annual inflation rate of about 67 percent.Cheap gasoline has been viewed for generations as a birthright in Iran, sparking mass demonstrations as far back as 1964, when a price increase forced the shah to put military vehicles on the streets to replace those of striking taxi drivers.

. India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy rainfall over North Eastern parts of India during the next two days.According to IMD, similar weather conditions are also likely to prevail over Bihar, East Madhya Pradesh, East Uttar Pradesh, Odisha and West Bengal today. Meanwhile, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Bihar, Odisha, Sub Himalayan West Bengal, Sikkim and Telangana are expected to witness thunderstorms accompanied with lightning and gusty winds during the next two days.The Met Department has also predicted hot and humid weather over Kerala and Mahe today.

. Union Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal today called for India to build on its position as the pharmacy of the world and emerge as a global medical and healthcare destination. Addressing the inauguration of Pharma Mach Tech and Labnext Expo 2026 in New Delhi, Mr Goyal highlighted the growing importance of healthcare beyond treatment, encompassing prevention, wellness, caregiving, medical devices, telemedicine, teleconsultation, innovation and research and development for newer drugs and modern equipment. The Minister also urged the industry to utilise the opportunities arising from India’s free trade agreements. Mr Goyal called upon stakeholders to participate in the country’s development journey and work towards ensuring access to quality education, healthcare and opportunities for all. He said that the medical and pharmaceutical machinery, consumables and related sectors represent a growing field with significant potential to create crores of jobs, thousands of business opportunities and lakhs of new startups, particularly in the medtech field.The Minister also called for strengthening the startup incubation ecosystem for medtech, medical equipment and consumables, along with improvements in design, copyrights, patent laws and the intellectual property ecosystem. Emphasising the need for self-reliance in research, medicines and medical equipment, Mr Goyal called for technology partnerships, stronger buyer-seller relationships and joint ventures to advance self-reliance in the sector. The Minister said India should aim not only to provide high-quality healthcare to every Indian but also to provide wellness and healthcare services to the world from India.

. India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy rainfall over Bihar, East Madhya Pradesh, East Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, West Bengal and North Eastern parts of the country during the next two days. IMD said that thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds are likely to prevail over Andhra Pradesh, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Bihar, Jharkhand, Karnataka, Odisha, Sub-Himalayan West Bengal and Sikkim tomorrow. Meanwhile, Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Kerala and Mahe are expected to experience hot and humid weather till 8th of this month.

. The Goa Government will launch the ‘Goa Ujjwala Scheme’ on September 5, providing financial assistance equivalent to the cost of three domestic LPG cylinders every year to eligible household LPG and PNG consumers. Chief Minister Dr. Pramod Sawant said ₹3,000 will be directly transferred into beneficiaries’ bank accounts through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT).The Civil Supplies Department has made a provision of ₹100 crore for the scheme. There is no income criterion for availing the benefit. However, only one domestic gas connection per family will be eligible. Existing Griha Aadhar and Deen Dayal Social Security Scheme beneficiaries can apply by submitting the scheme application and bank passbook. A separate application will be available for open-category beneficiaries. Applications will be available at panchayat and municipal offices. The first instalment is expected to be credited to beneficiaries’ bank accounts on September 9 or 10.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will share his thoughts with the people of the country and abroad in the Mann Ki Baat programme on Akashvani at 11 AM on Sunday. It will be the 137th episode of the monthly radio programme. The programme will be broadcast across the entire Akashvani and Doordarshan network, the AIR News website, and the Newsonair mobile app. It will also be live-streamed on the YouTube channels of AIR News, DD News, the PMO, and the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting. Akashvani will broadcast the programme in regional languages immediately after the Hindi broadcast.

. Luxembourg Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Xavier Bettel has backed India’s bid for a permanent seat in the United Nations Security Council (UNSC), saying the body must be reformed to reflect the realities of the present global order.In an interview with a news agency, Mr Bettel said India’s size and global importance make its inclusion in an expanded Security Council necessary. He said the UNSC could be expanded to include major countries that currently do not have a permanent role, citing India and Brazil. Mr Bettel also criticised the existing veto system, describing it as a “relic of the Second World War” and arguing that no single country should have the power to block decisions supported by the wider international community.He proposed that a two-thirds majority in the Security Council should be able to override a veto, calling for a more representative and democratic decision-making process. Mr Bettel is on a three-day official visit to India.

. The Archaeological Survey of India has notified Gollala Gudi Temple at Palampet in the Mulugu district of Telangana as a monument of national importance. The Ministry of culture said that the temple is situated near the UNESCO listed Ramappa Temple and is renowned for its exquisite carvings and architectural heritage.The temple is a Trikutalaya and consists of a mandapa facing East and surrounded by three garbhagriha.A monument of national importance in the country is protected under the Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act, 1958. The Archaeological Survey of India takes charge of such sites for conservation, maintenance, and regulated public access

. At the China Masters badminton, Indian men’s doubles pair of Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty entered their fourth-straight China Masters semifinal after beating Denmark’s Kim Astrup and Anders Skaarup Rasmussen 21-13, 16-21, 21-18 in Shenzhen this evening.The Indian pair defeated France’s Toma Junior Popov and Christo Popov 21-17, 22-24, 21-9, last night, to make it to the quarterfinal.In men’s singles Kidambi Srikanth’s campaign at the China Masters, ended after losing 16-21, 16-21 to Lee Cheuk Yiu of Hong Kong in the quarterfinals in Shenzhen today.Earlier, India’s women’s singles campaign came to an end yesterday after Tanvi Sharma lost 21-17, 18-21, 21-16 against Japan’s Tomoka Miyazaki.

. India has joined the United States and 24 other countries in an international initiative aimed at shaping the development of next-generation 6G networks.In a social media post, the US Department of Commerce said, India had joined the US and 24 other countries in an effort to ensure that next-generation networks reflect shared security interests, strengthen competitiveness and drive innovation.The announcement came after Union Minister of State for Commerce and Industry Jitin Prasada met US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick on the sidelines of the G20 Innovation Ministerial. The two leaders discussed the future of 6G technology and the importance of international cooperation in developing next-generation telecommunications networks.During the meeting, India and the US discussed strengthening cooperation in semiconductors, AI and data centres. MoS Prasada encouraged the possibility of more US investments in ISM 2.0, proposed strengthening AI technology partnership and shared a mechanism for safeguards for AI. Jitin Prasada led the Indian delegation at the G20 Innovation Minister’s meeting held on September 1 and September 2 in Chapel Hill, North Carolina, United States, hosted by the US Department of Commerce and the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy (OSTP).The meeting concluded with the G20 Innovation Ministerial Statement, highlighting the potential of emerging technologies to drive prosperity, productivity and opportunity. India reaffirmed its commitment to building strategic partnerships in AI, semiconductors, DPI, robotics and other emerging technologies into greater opportunities for innovation, economic growth and an improved quality of life for its citizens.

. India’s foreign exchange reserves surged by 11.4 billion US dollars to a record high of 740.8 billion dollars during the week ended 28th of last month.According to the Reserve Bank of India data, Foreign currency assets, the largest component of the reserves, increased by 9.3 billion US dollars to 600.6 billion dollars during the week. Gold reserves added 2.1 billion dollars to 116.4 billion dollars.However, Special Drawing Rights declined by 43 million dollars to 18.8 billion dollars. Country’s reserve position with the International Monetary Fund dipped 11 million dollars to 4.9 billion dollars.

. In Asian markets today, South Korea’s Kospi surged 4.6 per cent, while Japan’s Nikkei 225 gained 2.1 per cent.In European markets, Germany’s DAX was trading 0.4 per cent down, while London’s FTSE 100 added 0.1 per cent, when reports last came in.Meanwhile, stock markets in the United States will remain closed tonight on account of a holiday.

. Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla has said that thirty-three per cent reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies will open new avenues for women’s political leadership. Mr Birla said that the coming years would witness a new generation of women leaders emerging across political, administrative, and social spheres.The Lok Sabha Speaker stated this while inaugurating a two-day All-India Capacity Building Workshop on the theme -Gender-Responsive Governance, organized by the National Commission for Women at Faridabad, Haryana today. He mentioned that the focus must now shift from merely providing support and opportunities to women towards enabling them to actively shape policies, programmes, and laws. Mr Birla said, India cannot progress towards the goal of a developed nation without the economic and social empowerment of its women, who constitute nearly half of the country’s population. He called upon women legislators to deliberate on effective policies, schemes, and legislative measures that can strengthen women economically and socially, particularly those facing deprivation and hardship. Emphasizing the importance of dialogue in a vibrant democracy, Mr Birla said that the challenges and aspirations of the people are best addressed through continuous discussion and consultation. Referring to the constitutional commitment to equality and various legislative measures undertaken for women’s safety, empowerment, and self-reliance, he highlighted that institutions such as the NCW have an important role in identifying emerging challenges and facilitating solutions.

. In Women’s Cricket, India defeated Pakistan by seven wickets in the Women’s Asia Cup T20 match in Dubai. Pakistan were bowled out for just 55 in 18.1 overs, their lowest-ever total in T20 Internationals.Young spinners Shree Charani and Prema Rawat took three wickets each, while Deepti Sharma claimed two. India chased down the target in 8.4 overs, with captain Harmanpreet Kaur remaining unbeaten on 18. The match also marked Harmanpreet’s 150th T20 International as India’s captain, making her the first international captain, male or female, to reach the milestone.Pakistan started confidently at 27 without loss but lost six wickets for just nine runs as India’s spinners took complete control. Charani returned figures of three for seven, while Rawat took three for nine. India’s bowlers bowled 78 dot balls in Pakistan’s innings and never allowed the opposition to recover. India have now won seven of the eight T20 Asia Cup meetings against Pakistan.

. Minister of State for External Affairs, Kirti Vardhan Singh interacted with the Indian community in Saudi Arabia during his visit to the country. In a social media post, he informed that the meeting took place at an event organised by the All-India Steering Committee under the patronage of the Embassy.Mr Singh lauded the Indian community’s invaluable contribution to strengthening India and Saudi Arabia ties across trade, investment, energy and culture. He also encouraged them to contribute to the realisation of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s vision of a Viksit Bharat 2047.

. The Indian Embassy in China has requested the families of Indian nationals who remain missing in the devastating mudslide and flash flood last month, to submit DNA samples to assist in the identification process. The Embassy in a statement said, families willing to provide DNA information are requested to submit the relevant data, in the internationally-recognised CODIS format to the Embassy of India. The Embassy will forward the data to the concerned Chinese authorities for comparison. The Embassy will be notified and will in turn inform the family, should a match be confirmed. Families may contact the Embassy of India through Telephone, +86 18514284905 and Email, cons1.beijing@mea.gov.in.Last month, the Tibet Autonomous Region of China and Bagmati province of Nepal had faced deadly flash floods.

. International Monetary Fund. IMF, Deputy Managing Director Nigel Clark acknowledged India’s economic performance, resilience and growth track record in the current global scenario, and Government’s efforts for fiscal consolidation and support measures in the aftermath of the West Asian crisis.Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman today met Mr. Nigel Clark in New Delhi.The Ministry of Finance said that they both discussed India-IMF relations, with appreciation for India’s role in supporting IMF South Asia Regional Training and Technical Assistance Center. It said that both sides emphasised the importance of continued India-IMF engagement in strengthening macroeconomic cooperation, supporting sound policies and contributing to greater regional and global economic resilience. They also discussed the outlook for India and the global economy, including the nation’s evolving growth trajectory and the implications of ongoing shifts in the global economic environment, including India’s trade agenda and developments in the global trading system including recently concluded bilateral trade agreements.

. The US trade deficit in goods and services surged 24.4 per cent in July, to 88.6 billion US dollars. That is higher than the upwardly revised figure of 71.2 billion US dollars recorded in June, according to data from the US Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) and the US Census Bureau. The increase came as US imports rose, while exports declined. Exports fell 2.1 per cent to 310.7 billion US dollars, while imports climbed 2.8 per cent to 399.3 billion US dollars.The US also recorded a five-billion-dollar goods trade deficit with India in July. The largest US goods trade deficit was with Mexico, at 27.5 billion US dollars, followed by Vietnam, Taiwan, China, South Korea and the European Union. The services sector provided a relatively small offset to the widening goods deficit. Services exports declined by 0.4 billion billion US dollars to 109.7 billion, while services imports fell by 0.6 billion US dollars to 78.7 billion.

. In Pakistan, sixteen people were killed and over 70 injured in separate road accidents in Punjab and Sindh provinces.Seven persons lost their lives, and over 50 were injured when a tractor trolley carrying wedding party guests collided with an overspeeding trailer at Sardar Garh area in Punjab province. The injured were shifted to local hospital where condition of five of them is stated to be critical.The second accident occurred at Thal city in Sindh’s Jacobabad district when a passenger bus en route to Lahore veered off the road due to overspeeding and rammed into a tree, claiming lives of nine passengers. The injured were shifted to a local hospital where the condition of four is critical.

. In Tennis, India’s Karan Singh clinched the Men’s Singles title at the ITF Men’s World Tour M15,  at Bali in Indonesia. This is Karan’s fourth career title and his third of the 2026 season — second in singles.  The fourth-seeded Indian who hails from Karnal in Haryana defeated the fifth seed Isaac Becroft of New Zealand in a closely contested final on hard courts, clinching a 7-5, 7-6 (3) win to lift the title.The singles victory in Indonesia marks a highly successful continuation of Karan’s 2026 calendar, coming just weeks after he clinched the doubles title at the ITF M15 Astana in Kazakhstan.The 23-year-old Karan has won one ATP Challenger doubles title at the 2024 Brazzaville Challenger with Florent Bax.

. In Badminton, Indian pair Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty clinched the men’s doubles title at the China Masters in Shenzhen today. The Indian duo defeated China’s He Ji Ting and Ren Xiang Yu 11-21, 21-13, 21-17 in the summit clash to secured India’s first-ever title at the China Masters.The victory marks the duo’s second title of the season. They had earlier won the Singapore Open Super 750 and finished runners-up at the Thailand Open Super 500. Satwik and Chirag booked their place in the final after defeating Malaysia’s Nur Mohd Azriyn Ayub and Tan Wee Kiong 21-15, 18-21, 21-11 in the semifinals. The Indian duo had finished runners-up at the China Masters in 2023 and 2025 and reached the semifinals in 2024.

. In Shooting, the Indian team will be attending its final training camp ahead of the Asian Games 2026 starting later this month in Japan. The camp begins at the Madhya Pradesh State Shooting Academy in Bhopal today.A total of 18 shooters, including nine men and nine women, will be taking part in the camp. The squad includes top shooters such as Manu Bhaker, Esha Singh, and Aishwary Pratap Singh Tomar.Expert coaches will be training the shooters in rifle and pistol events. The camp will be focusing on shooting skills, fitness, recovery, and mental strength. The shooters will also be training at modern 10, 25, and 50-metre ranges.A special training camp was held in Bhopal last month as well. The Indian shooting team will leave for the Asian Games after the camp concludes on 14th September.

. The Government has announced the Tenzing Norgay National Adventure Awards for the year 2024. The awards recognise outstanding achievements by individuals in the field of adventure and seek to promote a spirit of endurance, risk-taking, teamwork and quick and effective decision-making in challenging situations. The awards are given in four categories, which are Land Adventure, Water Adventure, Air Adventure and Lifetime Achievement. Each awardee will receive a statuette, a certificate and award money of 15 lakh rupees. The awardees are Baljeet Kaur and Skalzang Rigzin in Land Adventure category, Rimo Saha in Water Adventure category and Shiv Prasad Chamoli in the Life Time Achievement category.The selections were made following the recommendations of the National Selection Committee. The Committee evaluated the nominations and recommended the awardees for conferment of the national honour.The awards seek to promote among the youth a spirit of courage, endurance, discipline, risk-taking and cooperative teamwork, while encouraging the ability to respond with speed and effectiveness in challenging situations. President Droupadi Murmu will confer the awards along with the National Sports Awards 2025. The date of the award ceremony will be announced later.

. The 5th Sohra International Half Marathon 2026 was successfully held today, bringing together regional, national, and international athletes to Meghalaya.The event was organised by the Meghalaya State Olympics Association (MSOA) in collaboration with the Directorate of Sports and Youth Affairs, Government of Meghalaya, Meghalaya Athletics Association and an official recognised by the Athletics Federation of India (AFI).The 2026 edition saw the registration of 11,672 runners across all categories. Participation included international athletes and runners from other states as well.In his keynote address,Wailadmiki Shylla, Minister, Department of Sports and YouthAffairs, Government of Meghalaya highlighted the event’s remarkable evolution from a modest starting field of 750 runners to nearly 12,000 participants.Welcoming athletes representing almost 24 states across the country, Shylla emphasized the marathon’s  widespread socio-economic impact, which directly benefits local homestay operators, transport providers, and farmers, while establishing Sohra as a top-tier sporting destination beyond its traditional fame for rainand waterfalls.Sukant Suki Singh, the first Indian to Complete three 200-Mile Ultramarathons, praisedMeghalaya’s exceptional sports infrastructure and natural beauty, identifying the state as the future sporting capital of India.He specifically commended Chief Minister Conrad K. Sangmafor completely transforming the region’s sports landscape and actively nurturing athletic talent from a young age.The Sohra Half Marathon witnessed strong performances across all its competitive categories, with Satish Kumar Verma emerging winner in the Elite Men’s 21 km category with a timing of 1:03:04, and Tejaswini Narendra Lambkane claiming the Elite Women’s title in 1:15:20.

. Vice President CP Radhakrishnan has said that the country today stands as an important place of transformation and renewed confidence, showcasing the results of collective determination and efforts. The Vice President said this after releasing a book titled Sankalp Se Siddhi ka Modi Yug written by Rajya Sabha MP Ghanshyam Tiwari. He said that whether it is advancing technology, building modern infrastructure, and strengthening national unity and promoting women-led development, education is the tool for empowerment. Mr Radhakrishnan also highlighted the contributions of the country’s youth, women, farmers, workers, and every citizen for their involvement in building a stronger and prosperous nation. He also underlined that Prime Minister Narendra Modi is the only leader in the world to provide free Covid-19 vaccines not only to 140 crore Indian people but also to hundred more countries.Speaking about the book, the Vice President said that through the publication, the author seeks to bring together many aspects of country’s larger narratives, reviving pride in cultural heritage and enhancing the country’s voice at the global stage. He added that the book reflects the journey of the nation and encourages everyone and boosts their enthusiasm.

. The Publications Division of the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting has received seven awards at the Federation of Indian Publishers (FIP) Awards for Excellence in Book Production, 2026. The Division’s journals, books and reference publications in Hindi, English and Urdu have been recognised in various categories.Director General, Publications Division, Dr. Dhiraj Kakadia said that the books and journals published by the Division play an important role in bringing diverse and valuable content related to national development, literature, culture, art and contemporary issues to readers. He said, the seven awards received by the Publications Division are a testament to the collective hard work, dedication and excellence of its officers and personnel.

In Badminton, Indian men’s doubles pair Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty will take on the Malaysian duo of Nur Mohd Azriyn Ayub and Tan Wee Kiong in the semi-final of the China Masters in Shenzhen today.The Indian pair defeated Denmark’s Kim Astrup and Anders Skaarup Rasmussen 21-13, 16-21, 21-18 in the quarter-final yesterday. With the victory, Satwik and Chirag reached the semi-finals of the China Masters for the fourth consecutive time.On the other hand their Malaysian opponents, Azriyn Ayub and Tan Wee Kiong, pulled off a major upset by defeating Indonesia’s world No. 7 pair, Sabar Karyaman Gutama and Moh Reza Pahlevi Isfahani, 21-17, 16-21, 21-19.The victory earned them their first-ever Super 750 semi-final appearance.Meanwhile, India’s campaign in the singles events came to an end as Kidambi Srikanth lost to Hong Kong’s Lee Cheuk Yiu in the Men’s Singles quarter-final. In Women’s Singles, Tanvi Sharma went down against Japan’s Tomoka Miyazaki.

. The 26th Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Summit in Bishkek has concluded with 13 key outcomes. The outcomes cover counter-terrorism, climate action, energy, disaster management and digital cooperation.The summit adopted the historic Bishkek Declaration, marking the SCO’s 25th anniversary. It also approved four MoUs and more than 20 decisions.A major decision was to include English as an official SCO language. Leaders also agreed to establish a Universal Centre for Countering Security Threats.The measures will strengthen cooperation against terrorism, extremism, organised crime and other transnational threats. They will also improve security information sharing.Several decisions focus on tackling drug trafficking and synthetic drugs. These include stronger coordination among law enforcement agencies and a cooperation programme on combating drug addiction until 2030. The measures support India’s efforts against cross-border narcotics trafficking and narco-terrorism.On climate and energy, SCO members agreed to enhance cooperation on energy conservation and efficiency. They also adopted a memorandum on combating climate change. These measures support India’s energy security and climate-resilient development goals.The summit also adopted a statement on assistance to countries affected by emergencies. It will strengthen cooperation in disaster management and humanitarian assistance, an area where India has significant capabilities.In the digital sector, members agreed to expand cooperation in artificial intelligence. The move will provide India an opportunity to share its digital and AI expertise and promote responsible and inclusive use of the technology.An agreement on information cooperation will also promote institutional exchanges and help strengthen India’s engagement with the regional media space.The Ministry of External Affairs said the outcomes give India a strategic platform to advance its positions on regional security, development and connectivity. They also strengthen India’s engagement with Central Asia and the wider Eurasian region.The MEA said, addressing the summit, Prime Minister Narendra Modi called for a roadmap for the next 25 years. He stressed the need for concrete outcomes in the areas of security, connectivity and opportunity.The two-day SCO Summit was held at Bishkek in Kyrgyzstan, from August 31 to September 1.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi today paid tribute to renowned Singer and former Member of the Assam Legislative Assembly, Bharat Ratna Dr Bhupen Hazarika on his 100th birth anniversary.In a social media post, Mr Modi said that Dr Hazarika’s voice carried the soul of Assam and the spirit of the Northeast to the entire nation. He noted that the legendary singer’s songs brought people closer and through his music, Dr Hazarika beautifully gave expression to the thoughts and aspirations of countless people.The Prime Minister also recalled attending the start of his birth centenary celebrations in Guwahati last year. He said that Dr Hazarika life and work will continue to inspire generations.Defence Minister Rajnath Singh today paid tributes to renowned Singer and former Member of the Assam Legislative Assembly, Bharat Ratna Dr. Bhupen Hazarika on his birth anniversary.In a social media post, Mr Singh said that Dr. Hazarika, a towering cultural icon and visionary, gave voice to the soul of Assam and enriched India’s cultural heritage through his music and profound humanism.The Defence Minister noted that Dr. Hazarika’s timeless compositions reflect the ideals of compassion, harmony and social justice, resonating with generations across the country.

On International Literacy Day, Education Minister Pralhad Joshi today said that literacy opens the door to knowledge, opportunity and a better future.In a social media post, Mr Joshi urged citizens to celebrate the transformative power of education and renew their commitment to ensuring that no one is left behind in the journey of learning. He said that an educated and empowered citizenry is the strongest foundation for a Viksit Bharat.

. Global crude oil prices climbed to near six-week highs as renewed strikes over the weekend in the Strait heightened concerns over supply disruptions. Brent crude was trading 1.1 per cent up at 97 US dollars and 37 cents per barrel in intra-day trade. West Texas Intermediate crude was trading 0.8 per cent up at 92 US dollars and 20 cents per barrel, when reports last came in.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi will visit Gujarat and Maharashtra today.In Gujarat, Prime Minister will lay the foundation stones, inaugurate and dedicate to the nation various development projects worth over 35 thousand crore rupees from Vadodara. Mr Modi will also dedicate to the nation three important sections of the Western Dedicated Freight Corridor (WDFC), marking completion of the project. Talking to media persons at Ahmedabad airport, Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said that this mega-project has now been fully completed and will be formally dedicated to the nation by the Prime Minister.A major highlight of the PM’s visit will be the dedication of three key sections of the Western Dedicated Freight Corridor spanning 326 route kilometres. Built at a cost exceeding ₹20,700 crore, this marks the full completion and operationalisation of the Freight Corridor network.The Prime Minister will also flag off freight train services from New Sanand, New Makarpura, New Umbergaon, and New JNPT, along with a new passenger train service between Tanda Road and Vadodara, connecting remote tribal regions of Alirajpur to the national rail grid.In addition, Mr Modi will also lay the foundation stone for three railway expansion projects worth over ₹9,700 crore and three National Highway projects costing around ₹1,780 crore to ease congestion and boost connectivity across Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh. He will also launch various civic and infrastructure projects of Gujarat Government worth ₹2,600 crore, including a 110 Megawatt floating solar plant at Kadana Dam and PMAY housing units. Later, the PM will also visit Navsari to inaugurate the BJP’s new AI-enabled, high-tech office in Navsari.”In Maharashtra, the Prime Minister will inaugurate the Global Fintech Fest (GFF) 2026 in Mumbai and address the gathering. The theme of GFF 2026 is, “Potential to Impact: Agentic AI, Tokenisation, Quantum – Trusted, Connected, Global Systems for Inclusive Finance.” The GFF 2026 seeks to build on India’s leadership in digital payments and financial inclusion and move from potential to impact. The discussions will focus on how AI, programmable finance, quantum technologies and other critical and emerging technologies can create trusted, inclusive and measurable outcomes for citizens, enterprises and economies globally.Since 2020, Global Fintech Fest has emerged as a leadership platform, bringing together policymakers, regulators, central banks, financial institutions, fintechs, technology companies, investors, academia and other global stakeholders to discuss and shape the future of finance. The seventh edition will run till 11th September 2026 in Mumbai.

. The Defence Acquisition Council (DAC) today cleared capital acquisition proposals worth over 1.10 lakh crore rupees for the defence forces. The approval was granted during a meeting of the Council held under the Chairmanship of Defence Minister Rajnath Singh. The proposals include, procurement of Chemical Biological Radiological and Nuclear (CBRN) Recce Vehicles, High Mobility Vehicles (HMV), Self-Propelled Mechanical Mine Layers (MML), Advanced Light Helicopters (ALHs), Trawl Tanks and Sarvatra Bridge System for the Indian Army. For the Indian Navy, Acceptance of Necessity was accorded for the procurement of Arudhra Radars, Design and Development and subsequent procurement of Marine Gas Turbines (MGT). Arudhra Radar will replace the existing Air Route Surveillance Radars at various Naval Air Stations and MGT, a warship propulsion system, will reduce dependency on foreign vendors. Meanwhile, for the Indian Air Force, approval was granted to various proposals to enhance the war-fighting capability of fighters, transports and helicopters. Approval was also accorded for procuring Ground-Based Multi-Purpose Jammer (GBMPJ) and installing Defence Forces Secure Access Card (DEFSAC) System.Defence Ministry said that 98 percent of total procurements will be made from the Indian Industry. The CBRN Recce Vehicles will be capable of detecting, identifying, monitoring and marking of areas contaminated with CBRN agents. The HMVs will enhance operational capabilities, logistic support and mobility in challenging terrains. The MMLs will achieve the desired operational capability in terms of fast and responsive minelaying in difficult terrains. The ALHs will execute complex missions across all terrains and operational situations for the Indian Army and the Indian Air Force. The Trawl Tanks and Bridge System will be utilised to provide composite crossings to fighting formations during operations in varied terrains. The GBMPJ will provide effective jamming against radars of adversaries and DEFSAC will replace existing paper based Identity Card, Passes, Permits with an interoperable Radio Frequency Identification-based smart cards system.

. Wall Street ended higher yesterday, after Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said he would be inclined to support holding rates steady barring any surprises in upcoming inflation data. Among the major indices, the Nasdaq Composite surged 1.4 per cent the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 1.2 per cent, and the S&P 500 gained 1.1 per cent.On the economic front, the unemployment insurance weekly claims increased by 2,000 to 2 lakh six thousand in the week ending August 29, according to the data released by US Department of Labour.Market participants closely watch the upcoming nonfarm payrolls data to gauge the Federal Reserve’s next policy stance.

. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh will be on a three-day official visit to Sri Lanka, starting today. In a social media post, Mr. Singh highlighted that besides the longstanding partnership as well as deep historical and civilisational ties, Sri Lanka is one of India’s most important partners under the Neighbourhood First and MAHASAGAR initiatives.He added that he is looking forward to a productive engagement with the leadership of Sri Lanka. The Defence Minister will also interact with the vibrant Indian diaspora in Sri Lanka during the visit.
